did_you_know.text: The widow who appealed to Elisha was part of the community of the prophets. Her husband had died fearing the Lord, but his debts had left their two children in danger of being taken as slaves.
Elisha asked not only what the widow lacked, but also what she already had in her house. She replied that she had nothing except a small jar of oil.
Elisha instructed the widow to ask her neighbors for empty containers, emphasizing, “Do not ask for just a few”—she was not to settle for only a small number of containers.

The miracle of the oil took place inside the house, with the door closed and the mother and her sons alone. As long as there were containers, the oil continued to flow; when the containers ran out, the oil stopped as well.
The woman from Shunem recognized Elisha as “a holy man of God.” Because of her hospitality, she and her husband prepared an upstairs room for him with a bed, a table, a chair, and a lamp.
The Shunammite woman had not asked Elisha for a son, and she even reacted anxiously to his words. Nevertheless, the promise came true: a year later, she became pregnant and gave birth to a son.
When her son died, the Shunammite woman was not satisfied with Gehazi going ahead with Elisha’s staff. She swore that she would not leave Elisha until he personally went with her.
After Elisha prayed and carried out his actions in the room, the child sneezed seven times and opened his eyes. Elisha called the boy’s mother and returned her son to her.

During the famine, the sons of the prophets prepared a stew from fruit gathered from a wild vine, without knowing what it was. When they realized that the stew was dangerous, they cried out, “There is death in the pot!”
A man from Baal-shalishah brought Elisha twenty barley loaves and fresh grain. According to the word of the Lord, the food was enough for a hundred people, and some was left over.
